summary:
**Conversation Overview**

Steve Schneider is a faculty member at SUNY Polytechnic Institute working across teaching, research, and institutional initiatives in AI literacy and related fields. He came to this conversation seeking help designing a personal project management system from scratch, having previously tried tools like Microsoft Planner without success. His core problem: everything is driven reactively by email and calendar with no bird's-eye view across overlapping projects. He identified Claude conversations as his natural planning habitat, leading to a workflow design where Claude serves as the thinking and structuring partner, with outputs living in an Excel/SharePoint spreadsheet as the execution artifact.

The conversation established a complete project taxonomy for Steve's work. Eight courses were identified and named by course number as stable slugs: COM375, IDT575, COM216, IDT507, IDT555, AI188, STS188, POS110, each split into two project phases — Develop and Deliver — with delivery semesters ranging from Fall 2026 through Fall 2028. Projects were organized into typed categories: Research (HERC — Herkimer County AI initiative, deadline Nov 15 2026; DACAC — Analytic Capabilities project, opens March 18 2026, deadline May 15 2027), Conferences (AACUU with co-lead Diane Schichtman, deadline Apr 10; SUNYG workshop in Saratoga Apr 8–10; STONY — Stony Brook visit to meet Shyam, Apr 14–16; NYHIM — NYHIMA plenary and 3-hour workshop, June 2026), Presentations (AIFWB — AI Fellows Research Webinar with Michelle, March 30), Institutional (AFRICA — Nigeria/Cameroon trip deadline June 1; BCSYN — Brightspace~Claude Hackathon, three Wednesdays starting March 25, urgent), and One-offs (AIXOH — AIX Open House posters March 25 reused March 30). A five-character slug convention was adopted for project IDs. Verb-named project titles were established as the standard (e.g., "Complete," "Deliver," "Submit," "Attend") to make end states explicit.

The system architecture agreed upon: planning and iteration happens in Claude conversations, which serve as the reasoning trail; outputs are generated as XLSX files dropped into SharePoint, where they live as the execution surface. Steve works in the spreadsheet directly for small updates; returns to Claude when replanning is needed. The master sheet columns are: Slug, Project Name, Type, Lead, Deadline, Status, Purpose/Main Task, Notes. Steve prefers Google Sheets interface but is staying Microsoft 365/SharePoint-centric for ecosystem consistency. The conversation ended with Steve preparing to generate the master XLSX via Claude Code on his desktop, with the understanding that he should paste the project list naturally into Claude Code rather than use formatted markdown prompts.

Your courses integrate RTW across platforms over semester arcs. The 4-6 module OER structure suggests more discrete, standalone exercises.
